See acceptance coverage, admin/observability measurements and recorded fixture measurements.

docs.title: Reproduce the routine checks
docs.text:
make check
mvn -B verify
make frontend-check
python3 scripts/e2e.py
python3 scripts/check-public-content.py

Set LINHA_TEST_DATABASE to a disposable PostgreSQL database for integration checks; otherwise those scenarios are explicitly skipped. Tests create/remove isolated schemas.

LINHA_TEST_DATABASE='postgres://user:password@localhost/linha_test?sslmode=disable'   go test -race -count=1 ./server/...

The CI workflow supplies its database fixture and runs the contract, chart, publication, browser and restart suites. Cluster fixtures are separate; see run disposable Kubernetes validation.

docs.title: Limits of the evidence
docs.text:
Single-host Kind tests establish application coordination and recovery, not multi-node database, object-store or filesystem HA. Production IAM, admission policy, storage failures and capacity need tests in the target environment. Measured fixture latency is not an SLO or a maximum throughput guarantee.

The current database schema is 12. Older binaries can reject it; retaining IDs during migration does not make arbitrary binary rollback safe. Job metadata is retained indefinitely; payload retention and cleanup are separately configured.

docs.title: Queue recovery and browser renewal
docs.text:
Disposable PostgreSQL and signed HTTPS OIDC fixtures verify pending-request moves, original IDs and idempotency, immutable payload/result policy, repeated move audit, claim races, retry backoff, compatibility rejection, transaction rollback and cross-pool visibility. Refresh tests cover concurrent rotation across independent pools, encrypted credentials, changed membership and token bindings, UserInfo, transient provider failures, nonrenewable expiry and logout.

Browser tests cover global and context-version selection, cancellation and moves, partial outcomes, viewer restrictions, searchable context suggestions, local date conversion and selection reset. These checks use local Docker fixtures; they do not assert deployment into an external Kubernetes cluster.

docs.title: Manage Spark applications
docs.text:
Configure driver capacity, executor allocation and Spark resources in the backend spec passed to ensureBackend. Linha creates one SparkApplication per managed driver. Kubeflow Spark Operator submits it, and Spark creates driver/executor Pods.

For a complete option list use SparkSettings, with separate tables for application/JAR arguments, drivers, executors, and Pod templates.

This guide assumes the operator watches the Linha namespace and your worker image contains the declared JVM main class and JAR. See deployment.

New driver Pods use <context-name>-<instance-id>-driver, for example reporting-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-driver. Linha lowercases the context prefix, replaces unsupported characters with hyphens and limits that prefix to 23 characters, keeping the complete unique instance ID within Kubernetes' 63-character name limit. A name with no supported characters uses context as its prefix. Existing applications retain their current driver names until a new instance is provisioned. No client configuration change is needed.

docs.title: Set the application and resources
docs.text:
{
  "image": "registry.example/workers/reporting:1",
  "engine": {
    "type": "spark",
    "version": "3.5.6",
    "settings": {
      "application": {
        "mainClass": "example.WorkerMain",
        "mainApplicationFile": "local:///opt/linha/worker.jar"
      },
      "drivers": {
        "minDrivers": 1,
        "maxDrivers": 3,
        "maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver": 2,
        "cores": 2,
        "coreRequest": "1",
        "coreLimit": "2",
        "memory": "10g",
        "memoryOverhead": "2g"
      },
      "executors": {
        "cores": 2,
        "memory": "4g",
        "memoryOverhead": "1g",
        "dynamicAllocation": true,
        "minExecutors": 0,
        "initialExecutors": 1,
        "maxExecutors": 8,
        "executorIdleTimeout": "60s",
        "cachedExecutorIdleTimeout": "120s",
        "shuffleTrackingTimeout": "120s"
      },
      "ui": {"enabled": true, "port": 4040}
    }
  },
  "results": {"type": "s3", "destination": "analytics"}
}

memory is the JVM heap, with memoryOverhead added to the container request and limit. A 10g heap plus 2g overhead gives the driver 12Gi. CPU requests and limits default to cores; override them separately when needed. Do not put -Xmx in javaOptions or override these resources through the main-container template. Defaults and bounds are in configuration reference.

The worker main method should use new SparkConf() to inherit submission configuration. Preserve Spark's driver/executor image entrypoint. Use application.arguments and javaOptions for application configuration, with Pod templates for files and environment variables. For driver JVM system properties such as -Dlog4j.configurationFile, see the JVM and Log4j example.

docs.title: Tune the driver pool
docs.text:
Set minDrivers and maxDrivers for capacity bounds. Use maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver to bound requests sharing one SparkContext. queueThreshold, waitSeconds and cooldownSeconds control driver growth; idleSeconds allows idle drivers above the minimum to retire.

Lost required drivers are replaced. With no live clients, the context version finishes accepted work and then stops all drivers, even when its minimum is positive. This lifetime behavior is described in architecture.

docs.title: Let idle executors retire
docs.text:
Enable dynamic allocation and set minExecutors: 0 if an idle application may have no executors. initialExecutors applies at startup; it is not a permanent minimum. Set finite cache and shuffle timeouts when their retained data should not keep executors indefinitely.

Default cache and shuffle timeouts are infinity. That is why an application can retain executors even after its visible jobs finish. Active tasks, cached blocks, shuffle tracking and the minimum count can delay executor removal. Finite retention can cause recomputation. Use ctx.cache and ctx.broadcast for request-owned resources; avoid globally clearing caches while other jobs run.

docs.title: Open a driver UI
docs.text:
Set ui.enabled: true, then choose a current driver:

kubectl -n linha get pods -l spark-role=driver
kubectl -n linha port-forward pod/<driver-pod-name> 4040:4040

Open http://localhost:4040. For ui.port: 4050, forward 4040:4050 instead. Each driver has its own UI and it disappears when that application stops.

The administrator console uses an ingress URL exposed by the SparkApplication when available. Linha creates no public Spark UI ingress or authentication proxy. The Spark UI is a separate service; configure its access policy separately. Use Spark event logs and a History Server for completed applications.

docs.title: Roll out a changed backend
docs.text:
Keep a logical name such as reporting. Ensure with the new image/settings and retain the returned context for the application process lifetime. Linha derives an immutable configuration version. Existing clients keep their version and accepted requests; new replicas attach to the new version. Close old contexts on graceful shutdown, or let their heartbeat expire after an unexpected exit.

Referenced ConfigMap and Secret contents do not enter the configuration hash. Use immutable names when a change must produce a new reproducible version. Only the primary worker image is resolved to a digest automatically; specify sidecar/init image digests yourself when required.

Read the upstream Spark configuration and SparkApplication guide for the engine-side behavior.

docs.title: Build a Scala client and worker
docs.text: This tutorial creates a Spark job, registers it in a worker, submits it through the client SDK, and restores its result using the saved job ID.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Use Java 17, Scala 2.12 and the matching com.k3rnl client, worker and Spark artifacts listed in the SDK reference.

You need a Linha deployment, Kubeflow Spark Operator and a worker registry that the deployment permits. Configure an S3 result destination named analytics and working server AWS credentials. Set up OAuth credentials for your application first.

The example uses a JSON result. File and dataset output uses the same submission flow.

docs.title: 1. Define the shared entrypoint
docs.text:
Put this code in a module shared by your client and worker:

package example

import linha._
import linha.json._
import linha.spark._
import linha.spark.syntax._

final case class RowsCount(value: Long)
final case class CountRows(size: Long) extends SparkEntrypoint[RowsCount] {
  def execute(ctx: LinhaJobContext[Spark]): RowsCount = {
    require(size >= 0)
    ctx.progress(0.1, "Counting rows")
    val count = ctx.spark.range(size).count()
    ctx.progress(1.0, "Finished")
    RowsCount(count)
  }
}
object CountRows {
  implicit val codec: EntrypointCodec[CountRows, RowsCount] =
    EntrypointCodec.derived("count-rows", 1)
}

The codec gives this business operation a stable handler name and wire version. The worker executes the class from its image; no class or closure is sent by the client. Compile this module before continuing.

docs.title: 2. Register the worker
docs.text:
package example

import linha.spark.SparkRuntime
import linha.worker.LinhaWorker
import org.apache.spark.SparkConf

object WorkerMain {
  def main(args: Array[String]): Unit = {
    val runtime = new SparkRuntime(new SparkConf(), sys.env("LINHA_CAPACITY").toInt)
    val worker = runtime.worker(
      sys.env("LINHA_SERVER_URL"),
      LinhaWorker.projectedIdentity(),
      Some(LinhaWorker.projectedCredentials())
    ).register(CountRows.codec)
    sys.addShutdownHook { worker.close(); runtime.close() }
    try worker.run()
    finally { worker.close(); runtime.close() }
  }
}

Package this main class and its dependencies into your worker JAR. The image must contain Spark 3.5.6 with Scala 2.12 and retain Spark's native container entrypoint. Place the JAR at /opt/linha/worker.jar, or update the application path below. The repository's example worker provides a runnable assembly and Dockerfile.

Push your image and verify that its repository is in Linha's allowedImages. Use compatible dependency shading: see compatibility.

docs.title: 3. Create the application client
docs.text:
import linha.CredentialProvider
import linha.client.LinhaClient
import linha.client.auth.CredentialProviders
import java.nio.file.Paths
import scala.concurrent.ExecutionContext.Implicits.global

val credentials = CredentialProviders.oauthClientCredentials(
  "https://identity.example/realms/jobs/protocol/openid-connect/token",
  "reporting-api",
  CredentialProvider.fileSecret(Paths.get("/credentials/client-secret"))
)
val client = new LinhaClient("https://linha.example", credentials)

Keep this client for the application's process lifetime. The mounted file contains an OAuth client secret; the SDK acquires the access token.

docs.title: 4. Ensure a context and submit
docs.text:
The example below selects a few settings. The backend reference lists the complete model; Spark settings lists every application, driver, executor and UI option with defaults and constraints.

import example.{CountRows, RowsCount}
import io.circe.parser.parse
import scala.concurrent.Await
import scala.concurrent.duration._

val spec = parse("""{
  "image": "registry.example/workers/reporting:1",
  "engine": {"type":"spark","version":"3.5.6","settings":{
    "application":{"mainClass":"example.WorkerMain",
      "mainApplicationFile":"local:///opt/linha/worker.jar"},
    "drivers":{"minDrivers":1,"maxDrivers":2,
      "maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver":2,
      "memory":"1g","memoryOverhead":"512m","cores":1},
    "executors":{"dynamicAllocation":true,"minExecutors":0,
      "initialExecutors":1,"maxExecutors":4,
      "memory":"2g","memoryOverhead":"512m","cores":1,
      "executorIdleTimeout":"60s","cachedExecutorIdleTimeout":"120s",
      "shuffleTrackingTimeout":"120s"}
  }},
  "results":{"type":"s3","destination":"analytics"}
}""").fold(throw _, identity)

val context = Await.result(client.ensureBackend("reporting", spec), 30.seconds)
val handle = Await.result(
  context.submit(CountRows(1000), idempotencyKey = "request-42"),
  30.seconds
)
println(handle.id)

Return handle.id to your API caller. The ID is durable; Spark processing may start later. The ensure operation can resolve an image and validate settings, whereas job acceptance waits only for its database transaction.

Keep the context while this process serves requests. Reuse the same name after configuration changes; Linha derives a version. Use a fresh business idempotency key for each new request, and reuse it when retrying the same acceptance.

docs.title: 5. Poll and retrieve
docs.text:
val state = Await.result(handle.status(), 10.seconds)
println(state)

Poll at your chosen interval until the state is SUCCEEDED, FAILED or CANCELLED. After success:

val result: RowsCount = Await.result(handle.result(), 30.seconds)
println(result.value) // 1000

result() retrieves an available result; it does not wait for execution. Use handle.attempts() to inspect persisted failures and handle.cancel() to request cancellation.

docs.title: 6. Restore the handle later
docs.text:
Create a new client with the same application identity and restore by ID:

val restored = client.job(savedJobId, CountRows.codec)
val retained = Await.result(restored.result(), 30.seconds)

This operation needs no active context or running driver. On application shutdown, close the context and client after stopping acceptance of new application requests:

context.close()
client.close()

Accepted work drains before Linha stops an unused context version. For the equivalent raw JSON route, see HTTP API.

docs.title: Requests, jobs and failures
docs.text:
These are the JSON objects used to accept a job and read its durable state. Ownership is derived from the authenticated API identity. A public ID is returned only after acceptance commits to PostgreSQL; it does not mean execution started.

{"handler":"count-rows","version":1,"payload":{"size":1000},"idempotencyKey":"request-42","retry":{"maxAttempts":1,"backoffSeconds":1}}

The same owner, logical context name and idempotency key return the original job when the normalized request and result policy match. Different content conflicts. An existing receipt remains replayable after its submitting version retires. Retries are opt-in and do not make user side effects exactly-once.

Field paths below are relative to their containing model; output fields have no caller default.

docs.title: State and retry semantics
docs.text:
State Meaning QUEUED Accepted durably; waiting for a compatible worker RETRYING Previous attempt failed/lost and an accepted retry remains; may be in backoff RUNNING A worker owns the current attempt under a lease CANCELLING Cancellation intent committed; completion is fenced out SUCCEEDED Verified result publication committed FAILED Terminal failure, deadline or exhausted retry policy CANCELLED Terminal cancellation

Queued/retrying cancellation is immediate. Running cancellation commits intent; the worker observes loss of execution authority, interrupts its handler and cancels the attempt's engine job group. Completion and cancellation serialize, so whichever commits first determines the allowed final transition. Terminal cancel requests return the retained state.

After lease/deadline loss, recovery marks an attempt lost and applies the accepted retry policy. A driver replacement alone does not guarantee a retry. Unsupported handler/version requests fail once a live ready backend establishes that no matching capability exists. Progress is current-attempt data, while attempt history remains available across server and worker restarts.

docs.title: Attempt
docs.text:
Output items from GET /v1/jobs/{job}/attempts. This endpoint returns {"items":[...]} without pagination. It records executions, including lost and failed attempts; retries retain the original job ID.

Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints id string Output Opaque attempt identity number integer Output Attempt sequence, starting at 1 state string Output RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, LOST or CANCELLED workerId string Output Worker that claimed this attempt startedAt RFC 3339 string Output Claim/start time finishedAt RFC 3339 string Optional output Terminal attempt time failure Failure Optional output Persisted diagnostics for this attempt

docs.title: SubmitRequest
docs.text:
Input to POST /v1/contexts/{context}/jobs; returned in Job.request. Requires X-Linha-Client-Lease.

Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints handler string Required; no default Stable registered handler name; executable code is installed in the worker image. Minimum length: 1. Maximum length: 256. version integer Required; no default Version of the associated protocol, handler or configuration. Minimum: 1. payload JSON value Required; no default Any valid JSON value understood by this handler; no remotely executable classes or closures. idempotencyKey string Required; no default Business acceptance key, 1–256 bytes, scoped to owner and logical context name. Minimum length: 1. Maximum length: 256. retry RetryPolicy Optional; omitted Bounded retry policy; omission disables retries beyond the initial attempt. deadline string (date-time) Optional; omitted Optional absolute RFC 3339 execution deadline. Recovery also fails queued/retrying work after it passes.

docs.title: RetryPolicy
docs.text:
Input at SubmitRequest.retry. Defaults to a single total attempt.

Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints maxAttempts integer 1 (also for 0) Total attempts including the first; default 1, range 1–10. Zero selects default. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 10. backoffSeconds integer 1 (also for 0) Delay before eligible retry, default 1 second; range 1–3600. Zero selects default. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 3600.

docs.title: Job
docs.text:
Owner-scoped output from acceptance, status, cancellation and listing.

Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints id string Present; no caller default Opaque server/resource identity; preserve it verbatim. contextId string Present; no caller default Opaque immutable context-version ID, not the logical context name. request SubmitRequest Present; no caller default Original accepted SubmitRequest; payload and retry policy remain durable. state string Present; no caller default QUEUED, RETRYING, RUNNING, CANCELLING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED or CANCELLED. docs.title: Published results and datasets
docs.text:
A completed upload is not yet a public result. The current fenced attempt must successfully publish verified output. Retained results can be retrieved by the same owner and job ID without attaching a context or starting an engine.

The descriptor kind is json, file, dataset or status. A status-only result has an empty files array and no dataset; Scala Unit entrypoints use this kind. JSON requires exactly one file; ordinary file results require at least one. Summed file bytes are bounded by the accepted maxBytes. Datasets retain a sealed manifest plus an immutable part inventory; total part bytes and manifest bytes are bounded separately. The supported dataset format is currently parquet. After payload retention expires, status/history remain and retrieval returns RESULT_EXPIRED. Physical deletion is separately opt-in.

Field paths below are relative to their containing model; output fields have no caller default.

Values: json, file, dataset, status. schema string Required; no default Stable application result schema identity, not an embedded JSON Schema document. version integer Required; no default Version of the associated protocol, handler or configuration. Minimum: 1.

docs.title: Application storage models
docs.text: Application storage exposes input files, shared data and temporary processing files through an explicitly permitted S3 destination. It is independent of retained job results: result expiry never deletes application files. An authorized context can access the entire configured destination prefix.

docs.title: WorkloadStoragePolicy
docs.text:
Input at BackendSpec.storage. An omitted storage object grants no application access. The server snapshots physical destination fingerprints into the context version. Configure operator access through S3Config.

{"storage":{"destinations":["application-data"]}}
Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints destinations array of strings Required when storage is present 1–16 unique operator-enabled aliases; each requires allowWorkloadAccess: true fingerprints map of strings Server output Alias → physical destination fingerprint; server replaces any caller value

docs.title: StorageSessionInput

docs.title: StorageSession
docs.text:
Output of successful session creation (HTTP 201). Clients are bound to a live client lease; workers are bound to their live attempt. A bearer token alone cannot revive expired authority. Destination changes invalidate old sessions.

Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints id string Output Opaque session identity token string Output credential Scoped bearer token used for session I/O, not the application's OAuth token destination string Output Captured destination alias root string Output Physical s3://bucket/prefix root uri string Output linha://{session-id}/ virtual root; credentials are separate

Use the Scala session API or the routes below. Session tokens and Hadoop options are scoped credentials: keep them out of durable job payloads and logs. Pass destination names and relative paths instead.

docs.title: Session I/O
docs.text:
Base: /v1/storage/sessions/{session}. Send the session token in Authorization: Bearer .... Query path is relative to the destination root. Names are at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes; traversal, empty interior segments, control characters, encoded paths and reserved _linha segments are rejected.

Method / suffix Inputs and output GET /stat?path=... StorageObject GET /list?path=... {"items":[StorageObject,...]}, at most 10,000 entries GET /data?path=... Byte stream; optional Range supports seek/range reads PUT /data?path=... Requires accurate Content-Length, at most 5 GiB; replaces the object POST /mkdir?path=... Directory marker; empty root is a no-op DELETE /delete?path=...&recursive=false Nonempty directories need recursive=true; root cannot be removed POST /rename?path=...&target=... Copy/delete; destination must be absent and outside the source subtree POST /lock?path=... Acquire 30-second directory lease; renew=true renews it DELETE /lock?path=... Release directory lease DELETE /close Revoke session; HTTP 204

Mutations return {"ok":true} except lock operations, which return {"leaseSeconds":30}. Recursive delete/rename inventory is capped at 10,000 objects. Copy/delete rename is not an atomic filesystem rename.

X-Linha-Storage-Lock identifies the locked directory for a protected write. Both source and target must stay within it. The SDK renews held locks every eight seconds and checks them before protected writes. Locks coordinate cooperating Linha writers; arbitrary external S3 writers are outside this protocol.

docs.title: Backend configuration
docs.text:
A backend is the worker image, engine configuration and storage policy submitted to POST /v1/contexts:ensure. In the Scala SDK this is the spec: io.circe.Json argument of LinhaClient.ensureBackend(name, spec); there is no typed Scala BackendSpec builder.

Follow the nested objects: BackendSpec → EngineSpec → SparkSettings → application / drivers / executors / kubernetes / ui. Results and application storage are separate backend settings.

Configuration area Reference Worker JAR, main class, arguments Spark application Driver count, request concurrency, CPU and heap Driver settings Executor count, allocation and retention Executor settings Environment, files, scheduling and sidecars Pod templates Retained outputs and path templates Result policy Input/shared application files Workload storage

Only fields documented for Linha's chosen adapter are supported. Spark's entire configuration namespace and the SparkApplication CRD are not accepted as a generic backend configuration object.

Field paths below are relative to their containing model; output fields have no caller default.

docs.title: Backend declaration examples
docs.text:
These examples ensure the same backend. The JSON tab is the HTTP body for POST /v1/contexts:ensure; the Scala tab uses the existing SDK and takes an already authenticated LinhaClient.

JSONScala 
{
  "name": "reporting",
  "spec": {
    "image": "registry.example/workers/reporting:1",
    "engine": {
      "type": "spark",
      "version": "3.5.6",
      "settings": {
        "application": {
          "mainClass": "example.WorkerMain",
          "mainApplicationFile": "local:///opt/linha/worker.jar"
        }
      }
    },
    "results": {"type": "s3", "destination": "analytics"}
  }
}

import io.circe.parser.parse
import linha.client.{LinhaClient, LinhaContext}
import scala.concurrent.{ExecutionContext, Future}

object BackendExample {
  def ensure(client: LinhaClient)(implicit ec: ExecutionContext): Future[LinhaContext] = {
    val spec = parse("""{
      "image": "registry.example/workers/reporting:1",
      "engine": {
        "type": "spark", "version": "3.5.6",
        "settings": {"application": {
          "mainClass": "example.WorkerMain",
          "mainApplicationFile": "local:///opt/linha/worker.jar"
        }}
      },
      "results": {"type": "s3", "destination": "analytics"}
    }""").fold(throw _, identity)
    client.ensureBackend("reporting", spec)
  }
}

Keep the returned context for the application process lifetime; it renews a client attachment. Close it when this process no longer submits work. For a complete worker image and main method, follow the tutorial and consult the Spark runtime API.

docs.title: Kubernetes Pod templates
docs.text:
Pod fragments live at engine.settings.kubernetes. Driver and executor templates are independent. The runtime container is named main; you customize its application environment and mounts while Linha/Spark own its lifecycle. See the Pod customization guide for procedures and Scala helpers for JSON/YAML loading.

Field paths below are relative to their containing model; output fields have no caller default.

docs.title: Allowed fragments and merge behavior
docs.text:
Each serialized template is at most 64 KiB. metadata accepts only labels and annotations. spec uses the Kubernetes v1 PodSpec field vocabulary from Linha's Kubernetes client version (v0.33.1). Consult the versioned PodSpec definition for upstream field types; the restrictions here also apply.

Structure Merge rule Objects/maps Recursive merge; client values override defaults containers, initContainers Recursive merge by unique name env, volumes, imagePullSecrets Replace matching entries by name volumeMounts Replace matching entries by mountPath Other arrays Replace the whole array

Null values and delete directives are rejected. Administrator legacy mounts, template defaults and client overrides form an effective snapshot for a new context. Referenced Secret/ConfigMap contents are not hashed: use immutable names when their contents must create a new version. Only the primary worker image is automatically pinned to a digest; pin sidecar/init images explicitly if needed.

Protected area Rule Top-level template No name, namespace, owner references or other fields outside metadata/spec Metadata keys No linha.io/, spark-, sparkoperator.k8s.io/ prefixes or app.kubernetes.io/managed-by Pod lifecycle No serviceAccountName, serviceAccount, automountServiceAccountToken, restartPolicy, ephemeralContainers or Pod-level resources Container main No command, args, image, workingDir or restartPolicy; CPU/memory use Spark settings Runtime environment No LINHA_ or SPARK_ names on main Mounts No overlaps with /opt/linha, /var/run/linha, /var/run/linha-pod-templates, /opt/spark/conf, service-account token mounts, including parent mounts Volume names No linha-, spark-, kube-api-access- prefixes Extra containers Unique valid names, image required in the effective template, image repository must be allowed Pull Secrets Valid names explicitly allowed by deployment imagePullSecrets or registrySecrets.allowedNames

Secrets, ConfigMaps and PVCs must already exist in the deployment namespace. Mount paths are absolute and normalized; effective mounts must reference defined volumes. The server identifies the offending field on validation failure.

{"driverPodTemplate":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"main","env":[{"name":"REPORT_MODE","value":"daily"}]}]}}}

docs.title: Result policy and paths
docs.text:
BackendSpec.results is snapshotted on job acceptance. It governs published JSON, files and datasets. Application storage has a separate lifecycle and is never deleted by job-result expiry.

maxBytes: 0 and retentionSeconds: 0 select their omission defaults. The enforced result limit is 5 GiB, including where older OpenAPI metadata describes a larger maximum. The server rejects a limit above 5 GiB during backend ensure.

Field paths below are relative to their containing model; output fields have no caller default.

docs.title: Provider-specific requirements
docs.text:
Provider Required selection Path behavior local root must exactly match the server's configured root Uses the default identity path; custom templates are rejected s3 destination must name a configured server alias Supports a version-1 custom relative template

All readers/writers of local results need the same persistent shared filesystem. An identical pathname on unrelated local disks does not provide durability. The server records an S3 destination fingerprint; changing bucket, prefix or endpoint under an existing alias makes retained access fail with DESTINATION_CHANGED. Credentials can rotate without changing that identity.

docs.title: Path placeholders
docs.text:
Default: {contextId}/{requestId}/{attemptId}/{file}.

Placeholder Meaning and placement {requestId} Public job ID; exactly once as a complete path segment {attemptId} Current attempt ID; exactly once as a complete segment {file} Output name; exactly once at the end, preceded by / {contextId} Optional context-version ID {submittedAt} Original acceptance time in UTC, default yyyyMMddTHHmmssSSSZ {submittedAt:yyyy/MM/dd} UTC date formatting with yyyy, MM, dd, HH, mm, ss, SSS and / - _ T Z literals 
exports/{submittedAt:yyyy/MM/dd}/{requestId}/{attemptId}/{file}

Templates and resolved names are at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Absolute paths, URI schemes, empty/./.. segments, control characters, backslashes, %, braces remaining after expansion, and segments starting _linha are rejected. Resolved allocations are persisted; downloads do not reevaluate templates.

Not used by local results. path PathTemplate Optional; omitted Relative path or path template as defined by this model; traversal is forbidden. maxBytes integer 67108864 (also for 0) Maximum accepted result bytes, default 67108864; enforced bound 1–5368709120 (5 GiB). docs.title: Spark settings
docs.text:
SparkSettings is BackendSpec.engine.settings when engine.type is spark and engine.version is 3.5.6. Managed deployments require application and use Kubeflow Spark Operator 2.4.0 (sparkoperator.k8s.io/v1beta2). Fields below are Linha settings, not an arbitrary SparkApplication or sparkConf passthrough.

For the Kubernetes resource Linha creates, see the upstream SparkApplication API reference (Operator v2.4.0) and Writing a SparkApplication guide.

Omitted driver/executor objects retain the defaults shown below. Explicit zero is retained for numeric Spark settings, then validated: for example minDrivers: 0 is valid, maxDrivers: 0 is invalid. Resource aliases have special rules below.

Field paths below are relative to their containing model; output fields have no caller default.

docs.title: Resource and allocation rules
docs.text:
Heap and overhead are binary MiB/GiB quantities even though Spark spells them m/g. memory: "10g" plus memoryOverhead: "2g" requests and limits a 12 GiB container with a 10 GiB JVM heap. Default overhead is rounded down to whole MiB, with a 384 MiB minimum. CPU requests/limits default separately to cores.

Dynamic allocation controls executors within a driver. Linha independently scales the number of drivers within the driver-pool bounds. One driver has one shared SparkContext; requests use separate SparkSessions, scheduler pools and attempt-specific job groups. Increasing request concurrency does not create more executor task slots. Cancelling one request targets its own job group.

Idle, cache and shuffle timeouts accept positive integer s, m, h, d durations up to 2147483647 seconds. Cache/shuffle timeouts also accept infinity. Equivalent values such as 1m and 60s normalize identically for version hashing. Timeouts are validated even with dynamic allocation disabled; they are applied only when enabled. Finite cache/shuffle retention can require recomputation.

{
  "drivers": {"minDrivers": 0, "maxDrivers": 3,
    "maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver": 2, "cores": 2,
    "memory": "10g", "memoryOverhead": "2g"},
  "executors": {"dynamicAllocation": true, "minExecutors": 0,
    "initialExecutors": 1, "maxExecutors": 8,
    "cachedExecutorIdleTimeout": "120s", "shuffleTrackingTimeout": "120s"}
}

This fragment belongs inside engine.settings alongside required application. Use new SparkConf() in the worker main method to inherit submitted settings. See driver main and image contract and Pod customization for environment, files and scheduling.

docs.title: JVM system properties and Log4j
docs.text:
Use spec.engine.settings.drivers.javaOptions for driver JVM flags, including -Dname=value system properties. It is a string of JVM options, not an array of main-class arguments. Linha passes it to the SparkApplication's spec.driver.javaOptions field. application.arguments is for arguments received by your main method.

For a custom Log4j 2 configuration, merge this fragment into engine.settings:

{
  "drivers": {
    "javaOptions": "-Dlog4j.configurationFile=file:/etc/job-logging/log4j2.properties"
  }
}

The file must exist at that path inside the driver container. Include it in the worker image or mount a ConfigMap through kubernetes.driverPodTemplate; see the file-mount example. Setting the property does not upload a client-local file. Spark's Log4j configuration example documents this system property and the explicit file: URI.

Multiple flags are space-separated in the same string. Use executors.javaOptions and an executor template mount separately if executors also need custom logging. Heap flags remain subject to the resource restrictions below. Changing JVM options changes the backend version: ensure the updated spec under the same logical name and submit through the returned context. Existing drivers keep their original version and JVM startup configuration.

docs.title: SparkSettings
docs.text:
Input at BackendSpec.engine.settings. Nested objects below specify every Linha-owned Spark option.

Spark 3.5.6 through Kubeflow Spark Operator v2.4.0. Memory is JVM heap; memoryOverhead is additional container memory. Deprecated memoryMi is an alternative heap alias.

Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints drivers object (fields) Optional; seeded defaults Driver pool, request concurrency and driver resources. Omission keeps the defaults in the nested table. executors object (fields) Optional; seeded defaults Executor resources and Spark executor allocation. Omission keeps the nested defaults. kubernetes SparkPodTemplates Optional; omitted Independent Pod fragments. Operator defaults merge with client overrides and are snapshotted in the version. application object (fields) Required; no default Required for managed deployment; JVM entrypoint already installed in the worker image. ui object (fields) Optional; omitted Per-driver Spark UI settings; does not configure Linha administrator UI.

docs.text: Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints drivers.memory string Optional; "1024m" JVM heap string in m/g units (case-insensitive), 512m–128g. Default 1024m. Explicit 0m is invalid. Pattern: ^[0-9]+[mMgG]$. drivers.memoryOverhead string Optional; max(384m, 10% heap rounded down to MiB) Extra container memory, 1m–128g. Default max(384, floor(heap MiB / 10)) MiB for managed SparkApplications. Pattern: ^[0-9]+[mMgG]$. drivers.memoryMi integer Optional; omitted Deprecated integer heap alias, 512–131072 MiB when nonzero; zero selects default. A nonzero alias cannot be combined with memory. Minimum: 512. Maximum: 131072. Deprecated. drivers.cores integer Optional; 1 Spark cores/task parallelism, 1–32; also the default CPU request and limit. Minimum: 1. Maximum: 32. drivers.coreRequest string Optional; corresponding cores CPU request string, positive and at most 32 cores. See JVM/Log4j example. -Xmx, -Xms and MaxRAM substrings are rejected; set heap through memory. drivers.minDrivers integer Optional; 1 Minimum drivers while clients have live leases; 0 is valid. docs.title: S3 destinations and administrator membership
docs.text: These models configure the server. Applications select destination aliases and submit backend declarations; they do not supply provider credentials or administrator membership.

docs.title: S3Config
docs.text:
Each value of LINHA_S3_DESTINATIONS is a destination configuration. Helm loads this JSON from s3.secretRef and s3.destinationsKey. Credentials use the server AWS default chain. The provider and its bucket are provisioned externally.

{
  "analytics": {
    "bucket": "example-results", "prefix": "linha", "region": "eu-west-1"
  },
  "application-data": {
    "bucket": "example-inputs", "prefix": "processing", "region": "eu-west-1",
    "allowWorkloadAccess": true
  }
}
Field Type Presence / default Meaning and constraints bucket string Required Nonempty bucket name without / or backslash prefix string Empty Relative base prefix, validated as a safe name; one trailing / is removed endpoint string AWS endpoint resolution Optional S3-compatible service endpoint region string us-east-1 Destination-specific SDK region pathStyle boolean false Enable path-style bucket addressing for compatible stores datasetRoleArn string Unset Role assumed for scoped distributed dataset writes; required for S3 datasets stsEndpoint string AWS endpoint resolution Optional compatible STS endpoint for dataset delegation allowWorkloadAccess boolean false Permit contexts to request application I/O across this entire destination prefix

Result identity hashes bucket, normalized prefix and endpoint. Credential rotation does not change it. Use a new alias when moving storage locations. Ordinary JSON/file results do not require STS. Distributed datasets require AssumeRole with enforced session policies, an allocation-scoped staging prefix and grants lasting at most one hour without mid-write renewal. Unsupported delegation returns DATASET_UNSUPPORTED; see dataset setup.

docs.title: Administrator request models
docs.text:
Administrator routes are a separate cross-owner surface under /v1/admin/. Viewer membership permits inspection; mutations require operator membership. Browser cookie mutations also require same-origin Origin and X-Linha-CSRF. Application OAuth identity alone does not grant administrator membership. See console procedures and public routes.

For POST /v1/admin/jobs/batch, malformed input changes no jobs. A valid batch returns HTTP 200 with independent per-item outcomes; failed items do not roll back successful items. Moves retain IDs, requests, original result policy, attempt counts and retry backoff. The destination must be active and match owner, logical name, engine type/version and source workload-storage access.

{"action":"move","targetContextId":"corrected-context-id","jobs":[{"id":"request-id","contextId":"old-context-id"}]}

docs.title: HTTP errors
docs.text:
Errors use an HTTP status and this JSON envelope:

{"error":{"code":"CLIENT_LEASE_EXPIRED","message":"a live client lease is required; attach to this context again"}}
Code / HTTP status Meaning INVALID_ARGUMENT / 400 Invalid fields, bounds or conflicting options UNAUTHORIZED / 401 Credentials missing or invalid FORBIDDEN / 403 Administrator role/action denied NOT_FOUND / 404 Missing or foreign owner-scoped resource CLIENT_LEASE_EXPIRED / 409 Attach again before accepting new work STALE_ATTEMPT / 409 Attempt or storage lock no longer owns its work CONFLICT / 409 Idempotency, receipt or resource conflict RESULT_NOT_READY / 409 Successful publication has not happened RESULT_EXPIRED / 410 Payload retention ended RESULT_TOO_LARGE, STORAGE_TOO_LARGE / 413 Configured result/object byte bound exceeded STAGING_LIMIT_EXCEEDED / 429 Concurrent staging reservation budget exhausted DATASET_UNSUPPORTED / 400 or 503 Provider lacks scoped delegation or dataset repository is unavailable DESTINATION_CHANGED / 503 Retained destination fingerprint differs SCHEMA_MISMATCH (SDK) Typed result descriptor does not match; thrown locally

Other adapter/storage errors can add codes. Inspect the structured code and HTTP status, not message text. Failure is persisted execution diagnostics; it is different from a transport error envelope.

docs.title: Operational observations
docs.text:
Operational models are read-only administrator observations across owners. They combine durable records with time-stamped engine/server observations. Check available, stale and observedAt before interpreting live resources or links. Observation does not attach a client or start an engine.

Page envelopes contain items and an opaque nextCursor; an omitted cursor ends the listing. Copy cursors unchanged. Overview counts are independent of page size.

docs.title: Managed worker protocol
docs.text:
These routes are used by managed worker runtimes, independently of application OAuth and browser login. Workers authenticate with their bound Kubernetes service-account token and X-Linha-Context-Id, X-Linha-Worker-Id, and X-Linha-Worker-Incarnation headers. Linha checks the live managed instance.

Operation Route Register / heartbeat / claim POST /v1/workers/register, /v1/workers/heartbeat, /v1/workers/claim Renew / fail / complete POST /v1/jobs/{job}/renew, /fail, /complete Allocate / upload POST /v1/jobs/{job}/outputs, PUT /v1/jobs/{job}/outputs/{output} Dataset access / register / seal POST /v1/jobs/{job}/outputs/{output}/access, /parts, /seal

Every attempt mutation carries the current worker ID, incarnation, attempt ID and fence, and requires an unexpired lease. Late writers cannot replace a retained result. Upload requests use X-Linha-Attempt and X-Linha-Fence headers instead of a JSON body. Claims only match a registered handler/version within worker capacity, with concurrent claims serialized by the durable queue. Attempt leases default to 30 seconds; the assignment carries the actual duration. SDK workers cancel locally on lease loss. See runtime API.

Claim query waitSeconds is an integer from 0–20, default 0. No assignment returns HTTP 204 with no body; the Scala transport represents this as Json.Null. Other successful receipts are:

Operation Output Registration {"registered":true} Heartbeat {"draining":false} (or true when draining) Renew {"leaseExpiresAt":"..."} in RFC 3339 Fail {"recorded":true} Allocate Allocation Upload ResultFile Complete Result

Registration does not let a worker choose its draining state; the server controls retirement. A repeated registration must preserve identity, capacity and capabilities. A retired incarnation cannot resume claiming by registering again.

Dataset part registration accepts 1–200 parts per raw request; the SDK uses batches of at most 100. Repeating a part path requires identical size/digest; sealing freezes the inventory. The seal format must be parquet.

The URL is the API HTTP(S) base, for example https://linha.example; credentials are evaluated when sending each request. Use one client for the application process lifetime. close() releases its attachments and stops lease scheduling.

docs.text: Packages linha and linha.client.auth. Application OAuth credentials, browser OIDC and managed-worker projected credentials are independent identities. This page covers JVM API clients; worker bootstrap uses its injected runtime identity.

docs.title: CredentialProvider
docs.text:
The interface defines bearerToken(): String. Providers can be shared across clients/transports. The server validates token claims; the provider only acquires and refreshes a bearer value.

Factory Return type Contract CredentialProvider.none CredentialProvider Empty token for explicitly anonymous deployments CredentialProvider.apply(get: () => String) CredentialProvider Calls application acquisition logic per request, validates nonempty token and hides nested acquisition errors CredentialProvider.static(token: String) CredentialProvider Fixed validated bearer token CredentialProvider.file(path: Path) CredentialProvider Rereads mounted token on each acquisition CredentialProvider.fileSecret(path: Path) () => String Rereads mounted OAuth client secret; pass this function to OAuth factory CredentialProvider.refreshing(acquire: () => AccessToken, clock: Clock = Clock.systemUTC(), refreshBefore: Duration = Duration.ofSeconds(30), retryDelay: Duration = Duration.ofSeconds(5)) CredentialProvider Synchronized expiry-aware acquisition; nonnegative timing arguments

Secret files are bounded to 65,536 bytes, trimmed, nonempty and reject control characters. Token values additionally reject embedded whitespace. Refresh occurs on use, with no background acquisition thread. The refresh window is the smaller of refreshBefore and one-fifth of the new token's remaining lifetime. A failed early refresh may reuse an unexpired token until expiry; retries respect retryDelay. An expired token is never returned as valid cached credentials.

docs.title: AccessToken and CredentialException
docs.text:
AccessToken(value: String, expiresAt: Instant) validates a bearer value and non-null expiry. Its public members are value and expiresAt; toString redacts the value. The refreshing provider rejects already-expired acquisitions.

new CredentialException(message: String, status: Option[Int] = None) contains the safe message and optional provider HTTP status. Bundled acquisition code excludes provider bodies, credentials and nested causes from these exceptions.

import linha.CredentialProvider
import linha.client.auth.CredentialProviders

object ApplicationCredentials {
  def provider(): CredentialProvider = CredentialProviders.oauthClientCredentials(
    "https://identity.example/token",
    "reporting-api",

}

docs.text: These helpers produce the same JSON as the language-independent backend reference. They do not introduce another backend model or upload local Pod-template paths to the server.

docs.title: SparkPodTemplates
docs.text:
SparkPodTemplates(driver: PodTemplate = PodTemplate.empty, executor: PodTemplate = PodTemplate.empty) is a public case class in linha.client.

json: Json yields {"driverPodTemplate":...,"executorPodTemplate":...}. withSettings(settings: Json): Json requires an object and sets its kubernetes member to this pair; it replaces an existing kubernetes member rather than merging with that member.

import io.circe.Json
import linha.client.{PodTemplate, SparkPodTemplates}

object TemplateExample {
  def settings(base: Json): Json = SparkPodTemplates(
    driver = PodTemplate.empty.withEnv("REPORT_MODE", "daily")
  ).withSettings(base)
}

The server merges deployment defaults and client overrides when creating a new immutable version. Changing referenced ConfigMap/Secret contents alone does not change that version; choose immutable object names for reproducible rollouts.

docs.title: ResultStorage
docs.text:
Object in linha.client, all functions return Json:

Signature Contract Local(root: String) / local(root: String) Local result policy; root must match configured shared root S3(destination: String, path: ResultPath = ResultPath.template(ResultPath.defaultTemplate)) S3 alias with validated version-1 path s3(destination: String, path: String) Lowercase helper with explicit template string; server validates the resulting policy

MaxBytes and retention can be set on the resulting JSON according to ResultPolicy; there are no extra typed constructor arguments for them.

docs.title: ResultPath and PathVariables
docs.text:
Package linha. ResultPath.template(text: String): ResultPath validates a version-1 template. Public members: version: Int, template: String and resolve(values: PathVariables): String.

PathVariables(contextId: String, requestId: String, attemptId: String, file: String, submittedAt: Instant) provides expansion values; submittedAt is acceptance time in UTC. Context, request and attempt IDs must each be a single safe segment; file can be a safe relative name. ResultPath.defaultTemplate is {contextId}/{requestId}/{attemptId}/{file}.

ResultPath.validateName(name: String): Unit validates relative names. Template, name and UTC token rules match path placeholders. Invalid paths raise IllegalArgumentException. The server persists the actual allocation; local resolve is not a way to authorize an arbitrary storage path.

docs.title: Scala Spark runtime
docs.text: Package linha.spark, artifact com.k3rnl:linha-spark_2.12. Spark 3.5.6/Scala 2.12 is provided by the worker image. See backend Spark settings for every deployment/resource option.

docs.title: SparkRuntime
docs.text:
new SparkRuntime(conf: SparkConf, capacity: Int) requires positive capacity. It creates one shared SparkContext with FAIR scheduling and bounded scheduler pool slots. Backend drivers.maxConcurrentRequestsPerDriver supplies the managed worker capacity; use sys.env("LINHA_CAPACITY").toInt rather than a different hard-coded slot count.

Member Return type Contract open(jobId: String) Spark Takes a slot, opens a separate SparkSession, sets attempt job group and scheduler pool on the execution thread release(value: Spark) Unit Clears thread-local group/session properties and returns the slot cancel(jobId: String) Unit Cancels only that engine job group worker(baseUrl: String, credential: WorkerCredential, credentials: Option[CredentialProvider] = None) LinhaWorker[Spark] Wires engine open/cancel/release and capacity automatically close() Unit Stops the shared SparkSession/SparkContext

When used through worker, the key passed as jobId to open/cancel is the unique attempt ID. Spark(session: SparkSession, pool: String) exposes session; the pool member is package-scoped. SparkEntrypoint[R] extends LinhaEntrypoint[R,Spark] with the same execute contract.

docs.title: Spark syntax
docs.text:
Import linha.spark.syntax._ for these extensions:

Extension Return type Contract ctx.spark SparkSession Request session from LinhaJobContext[Spark] ctx.cache(dataframe: DataFrame) DataFrame Reference-counted request-owned cache; released during cleanup, leaves pre-existing user cache alone ctx.broadcast[T: ClassTag](value: T) Broadcast[T] Broadcast destroyed during request cleanup ctx.results.parquet(dataframe: DataFrame, name: String, partitionBy: Seq[String] = Seq.empty) DatasetResult Distributed output with immutable published parts; partition names must be distinct existing columns

The public implicit extension classes are syntax.SparkJobContext and syntax.SparkResultWriter. Parquet writes use error-if-exists mode. Local writes probe shared mounts on executors; S3 writes require allocation-scoped STS grants and matching Hadoop/S3A magic-committer connectors. The helper inventories and hashes parts incrementally without collecting the DataFrame on the driver. At most 100,000 parts are accepted. See dataset prerequisites.

docs.title: Worker main and image contract
docs.text:
The worker image needs the declared application.mainClass and an image-local JAR at application.mainApplicationFile. Keep Spark's native container entrypoint. Bootstrap with new SparkConf() to inherit submitted settings; do not create a second independent SparkContext per request.

import linha.spark.SparkRuntime
import linha.worker.LinhaWorker
import org.apache.spark.SparkConf

object WorkerBootstrap {
  def runtime(): (SparkRuntime, linha.worker.LinhaWorker[linha.spark.Spark]) = {
    val spark = new SparkRuntime(new SparkConf(), sys.env("LINHA_CAPACITY").toInt)
    val worker = spark.worker(
      sys.env("LINHA_SERVER_URL"),
      LinhaWorker.projectedIdentity(),
      Some(LinhaWorker.projectedCredentials())
    )
    (spark, worker) // Register business codecs, run, then close worker and spark.
  }
}

Build/shade the application with matching SDK/Spark dependencies and the required connectors. The client/worker tutorial gives a registered entrypoint and runnable main sequence; compatibility records the supported image/toolchain choices.

docs.title: Scala application storage and Hadoop
docs.text: Packages linha and linha.hadoop. Application sessions are obtained from LinhaContext.storage(destination): Future[StorageSession] or LinhaJobContext.storage(destination): StorageSession. See the wire models and application-file guide.

docs.title: StorageSession
docs.text:
Construction is controlled by the SDK. Public values are serverURL, id, destination, root, and uri (all String). The session token is private; toString contains only destination and ID. Hadoop configuration necessarily contains its scoped bearer token and should not be logged or saved in payloads.

Member Return type Defaults and behavior relative(value: String) String Resolves relative, same-session linha://, or in-destination s3:// / s3a:// paths; rejects another session/bucket/prefix path(value: String) String Returns a credential-free linha:// session URI hadoopOptions Map[String,String] Filesystem class/cache flags plus session server/token/root/destination keys stat(value: String) StorageObject Object/prefix metadata list(value: String) Vector[StorageObject] At most 10,000 immediate entries open(value: String, offset: Long = 0L) InputStream Nonnegative offset; Range read when offset > 0; caller closes stream upload(value: String, source: Path) Unit Replaces object from local file, at most 5 GiB, through server staging mkdir(value: String) Unit Creates directory marker delete(value: String, recursive: Boolean = false) Unit Missing target is harmless; nonempty directories require recursive=true rename(source: String, target: String) Unit Copy/delete, target must be absent; not atomic lock(value: String, waitSeconds: Long = 120) session.StorageLock Directory lease; not destination root or duplicate local lock; retries conflicts every 250 ms until wait bound close() Unit Releases held locks, revokes session and removes local cache; cleanup errors can be thrown with suppressed secondary errors

StorageObject(path: String, directory: Boolean, size: Long, modifiedAt: String) is the public immutable metadata value; its fields match StorageObject JSON. Session calls are synchronous and blocking; API errors use LinhaException, path errors use IllegalArgumentException. Session validity depends on the live attachment or attempt. Reconstructing a session does not extend its authority.

docs.title: StorageLock
docs.text: Nested class StorageSession.StorageLock returned by lock. check(): Unit throws STALE_ATTEMPT when its locally tracked lease is lost. close(): Unit stops renewal and releases the server lock. The lease lasts 30 seconds and the SDK renews every eight seconds; a renewal error marks it invalid locally. Protected writes send the longest matching held directory lock. A stale lock cannot begin a protected publication; uncoordinated external storage writers are outside this guarantee.

docs.text:

Use normal context/job-context session acquisition in application code. These factories support Hadoop integration; they cannot revive an expired server lease.

docs.text:
Artifact com.k3rnl:linha-hadoop_2.12, class linha.hadoop.LinhaFileSystem extends org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem. The URI scheme is linha, with session ID as authority. session.hadoopOptions sets these configuration keys:

Key Value fs.linha.impl linha.hadoop.LinhaFileSystem fs.linha.impl.disable.cache true fs.linha.session.<id>.server Linha API base fs.linha.session.<id>.token Scoped session bearer token fs.linha.session.<id>.root Physical destination root fs.linha.session.<id>.destination Destination alias Public override/helper Behavior initialize(uri: URI, config: Configuration): Unit Requires linha://session-id/ and the session keys above getUri: URI, getScheme: String Initialized virtual root and linha scheme getWorkingDirectory: Path, setWorkingDirectory(path: Path): Unit Session-relative working directory getFileStatus(path: Path): FileStatus Metadata; synthetic block size 64 MiB, replication 1 listStatus(path: Path): Array[FileStatus] Directory entries, or the single file status open(path: Path, bufferSize: Int): FSDataInputStream Seek/range reads; negative seeks rejected create(path: Path, permission: FsPermission, overwrite: Boolean, bufferSize: Int, replication: Short, blockSize: Long, progress: Progressable): FSDataOutputStream Stages a local temporary file, uploads on close, maximum 5 GiB append(path: Path, bufferSize: Int, progress: Progressable): FSDataOutputStream Unsupported; throws IOException mkdirs(path: Path, permission: FsPermission): Boolean Creates marker via session delete(path: Path, recursive: Boolean): Boolean False for absent path; recursive behavior follows session rename(source: Path, destination: Path): Boolean Copy/delete; existing directory destination appends source basename, existing target returns false LinhaFileSystem.lookup(uri: URI): LinhaFileSystem Retrieves an already initialized filesystem for libraries without Configuration injection

HTTP 404 becomes FileNotFoundException; other API failures become IOException. Permissions, replication and block size arguments do not turn S3 into POSIX storage. Use a dedicated per-operation Hadoop configuration and close filesystem instances when done. Spark readers/writers use the same scoped session path; application files are not automatically retained as job results.

docs.title: Scala entrypoints and worker runtime
docs.text: Packages linha and linha.worker. See Spark-specific APIs for engine capabilities. Typed and raw handlers use the same JSON protocol.

docs.title: LinhaEntrypoint and EntrypointCodec
docs.text:
trait LinhaEntrypoint[R,E] defines execute(context: LinhaJobContext[E]): R. Code is compiled into the worker image; only parameters cross the API.

EntrypointCodec.derived[J: Encoder: Decoder, R: Encoder: Decoder: ClassTag](id: String, version: Int) creates EntrypointCodec[J,R]. Import linha.json._ for Circe case-class derivation. The generated descriptor uses schema id + ".result" and the same version; return type chooses status for Unit, file for FileResult, dataset for DatasetResult, and json otherwise.

The public case-class constructor also accepts id, version, descriptor, requestEncoder: Encoder[J], requestDecoder: Decoder[J], resultEncoder: Encoder[R] and resultDecoder: Decoder[R] explicitly. capability: Capability returns its registration contract; encodeResult(value: R): ProducedResult selects the runtime publication form.

docs.title: LinhaJobContext[E]
docs.text:
Member Return type Meaning jobId, attemptId String Durable request and current execution attempt engine E Request-scoped engine capability progress(fraction: Double, message: String) Unit Fenced persistence; finite 0–1 fraction, message at most 4096 bytes isCancelled Boolean Cancellation flag or local lease deadline exceeded checkCancelled() Unit Throws InterruptedException when execution authority is lost storage(destination: String) StorageSession Current-attempt application session; worker closes it during cleanup results ResultWriter Writer governed by the accepted result policy onCleanup(action: () => Unit) Unit Runs callbacks in reverse order after the attempt, before releasing the engine

Handlers should cooperate with cancellation; interrupting a thread cannot undo external side effects. Stale attempts cannot publish a replacement result. The base trait's storage/dataset defaults can throw UnsupportedOperationException; LinhaWorker provides these implementations when the server supports them.

Constructor arguments:

Token validation and live-instance checks remain server-authoritative.

RetryableJobException(message: String) explicitly marks handler failure as retry-eligible. Accepted maxAttempts still bounds execution. Ordinary handler exceptions are not retried by default; worker shutdown and selected transport errors can also produce retryable failures. Persisted diagnostics include phases, causes/suppressed errors and bounded stack traces; see Failure.

docs.title: Managed worker environment
docs.text: Linha injects LINHA_SERVER_URL, LINHA_CONTEXT_ID, LINHA_POD_UID, LINHA_CAPACITY, LINHA_SECURITY_ENABLED and LINHA_WORKER_TOKEN_FILE into managed workers. These provide runtime URL, identity, concurrency and projected credentials. Worker LINHA_MAX_STAGING_BYTES configures its positive staging reservation budget (default 5 GiB). Do not replace managed LINHA_/SPARK_ variables through the primary-container Pod template.

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text:
Release notes describe the behavior captured by each tag. Use the documentation version selector for releases published after the versioned site was introduced. Older release tags are not rebuilt automatically into new documentation snapshots.

  • 0.1.4: Complete categorized references, JSON/Scala examples and OCI Helm chart publishing.
  • 0.1.3: OAuth clients, application storage, queue recovery and renewable console sessions.
  • 0.1.2: reduce retired-resource Kubernetes API traffic.
  • 0.1.1: configurable provider TLS verification and simpler admin rules.
  • 0.1.0: initial durable job service, Scala/JVM SDKs, managed Spark engine, administrator console and Prometheus/Grafana integration.

Development pages can describe features absent from older artifacts. Do not apply new SDK examples to an older binary solely because its version is listed here.

docs.title: Linha 0.1.1
docs.text: Linha 0.1.1 adds configurable identity-provider HTTPS verification and simplifies administrator membership rules.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• security.oidc.tls.insecureSkipVerify and its environment equivalent default to false and apply only to identity discovery, signing keys and browser token exchange. Signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce and membership checks remain.
  • Viewer/operator rules inherit the configured browser issuer. Repeating it is optional; a conflicting issuer is rejected.
  • CI regenerates temporary fixture output instead of relying on cached test success, and pins Maven 3.9.9 for deterministic Central bundles.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
Update the server image and chart together to 0.1.1. No database migration or worker protocol change is required. Certificate bypass is optional; trusting the provider CA keeps TLS verification enabled. The server's setting does not change browser certificate trust.

This is a historical release. Current API/browser authentication fields differ; use the documentation captured with the version you deploy.

docs.title: Artifacts and verification
docs.text:
Images are ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server:0.1.1 and ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/spark-example:0.1.1. JVM artifacts use com.k3rnl, version 0.1.1, with sources, API documentation and signatures. The release includes the Helm chart and checksum.

Validation covered Go/PostgreSQL tests and race checks, browser sessions, Java 17 JVM builds, chart configuration, formatting, release preparation and specification validation. See the release comparison.

docs.title: Linha 0.1.2
docs.text: Linha 0.1.2 reduces Kubernetes API traffic from already deleted resources in retired context history.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Stop per-name probes for stopped contexts and dead instances.
  • Inventory managed Pods, Services and SparkApplications once per minute per server, including startup. An empty two-replica deployment needs six collection calls per minute, independent of retained history.
  • Preserve cleanup of late creates and leftover Services using persisted intent, reconciliation ownership and UID-conditional deletion.
  • Bound retries after inventory/deletion failure without interrupting active capacity, accepted-work draining, reactivation or retained results.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
Update every server replica to 0.1.2. This change needs no database migration, additional RBAC, SDK upgrade or business worker rebuild. Older replicas keep the previous polling behavior until replaced. Late orphan cleanup can wait until the next successful minute sweep.

The unreleased OAuth SDK and independent API/browser configuration described in development documentation are not part of this release.

docs.title: Artifacts and verification
docs.text:
Images are ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server:0.1.2 and ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/spark-example:0.1.2. JVM artifacts use com.k3rnl, version 0.1.2, with sources, API documentation and signatures. The release includes the Helm chart and checksum.

A fixture with 5,000 dead records and 100 controller ticks performs three inventory requests with no per-name probes. Tests also cover pagination, UID checks, competing controllers, late creation, failure backoff and reactivation. Go/PostgreSQL/race, JVM, restart and specification checks passed. See the release comparison.

docs.title: Linha 0.1.3
docs.text: Linha 0.1.3 adds renewable application credentials, storage access for workers, and administrative tools for recovering queues stranded on an unusable context.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• OAuth 2.0 client credentials in the JVM SDK, with expiry-aware concurrent token renewal. Public API JWT authentication and browser OIDC have independent settings.
  • Configurable browser OIDC scopes and clearer administrator membership diagnostics.
  • Application storage through explicitly authorized Linha destinations, scoped client/worker sessions, reusable resource locks and a new Hadoop filesystem SDK. Provider storage credentials stay on the server.
  • Status-only jobs that finish without allocating a managed result file.
  • Batch cancellation and movement of queued or retrying requests to a compatible context version, preserving request IDs, payloads, retry history and result policy.
  • Searchable context filters, local date/time inputs, page selection and centered confirmation dialogs in both global and context request views.
  • Encrypted OIDC refresh credentials shared across server replicas. Refreshed identity and group membership remain authoritative within the configured session lifetime.
  • Context-readable Spark driver names with full unique instance IDs, and a writable Ivy directory for Spark images running with arbitrary container UIDs.
  • A statically linked server binary validated inside its runtime image.
  • Standalone, searchable documentation with version snapshots on GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
This release changes authentication configuration. Configure API validation under security.api and browser login under security.oidc; administrator rules remain under security.admin. Application clients use OAuth client credentials and mount only their client secret when needed. See client authentication and administrator setup.

Back up PostgreSQL and stop the old server replicas before deploying all 0.1.3 replicas. Startup migrates the database to schema 12. Older binaries reject newer schemas; binary rollback requires restoring a compatible database backup. Requests and published result metadata remain durable across the upgrade.

Use matching 0.1.3 SDKs when rebuilding application clients and worker images. Application storage requires explicit destination opt-in and adequate server bandwidth and staging space. Application dataset files have a separate lifecycle from retained job results. See application storage.

Sign in again to obtain browser refresh credentials. Providers must issue refresh tokens; the absolute ui.sessionSeconds limit still applies. Existing Spark drivers retain their names until replaced, when the readable naming convention takes effect.

docs.title: Artifacts and validation
docs.text:
Images are ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server:0.1.3 and ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/spark-example:0.1.3. Maven artifacts use com.k3rnl, version 0.1.3: the parent plus protocol, client, worker, Spark and Hadoop SDK modules, with sources, API documentation, checksums and signatures. The GitHub release also includes the Helm chart and its checksum.

Validation covers Go/PostgreSQL and race checks, JVM SDKs, browser interactions, chart rendering, restart recovery, OpenAPI contracts, signed publication bundles and documentation builds. Hosted release workflows validate the tagged commit before publishing. External cluster and provider deployment policies still need validation in the target environment.

See the release comparison.

docs.title: Linha 0.1.4
docs.text: Linha 0.1.4 makes configuration and SDK information easier to find, with a categorized reference and a searchable index of public models and types.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Complete field references for backend declarations, Spark applications, driver/executor resources, Pod templates and result policies, including defaults, bounds and interactions.
  • References for requests, results, application storage, HTTP protocols, Scala/JVM SDK APIs, Helm values and server environment variables.
  • Shared JSON model definitions, equivalent JSON/Scala example tabs and direct links from guides to individual models and fields. Existing entry URLs and useful anchors remain available.
  • Driver JVM system-property and Log4j configuration examples, with links to the upstream SparkApplication API and guide.
  • Automated reference coverage checks for public models and nested fields, deployment settings and SDK families.
  • Public OCI Helm chart distribution at oci://ghcr.io/k3rnl/charts/linha, with an anonymous-pull check and chart-only recovery for existing releases.

Start at the reference index or Spark settings.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
Runtime behavior, public API fields and the database schema are unchanged from 0.1.3. There is no new configuration or database migration for this update. Applications using 0.1.3 can use the expanded reference without rebuilding their clients or workers. Upgrades from earlier versions must also follow the 0.1.3 upgrade instructions.

Published documentation snapshots remain frozen. Select 0.1.4 or latest to read the new reference.

docs.title: Artifacts and validation
docs.text:
Matching 0.1.4 artifacts include ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/server:0.1.4, ghcr.io/k3rnl/linha/spark-example:0.1.4, and the com.k3rnl JVM parent plus protocol, client, worker, Spark and Hadoop SDK modules. The Helm chart is available through OCI and as a GitHub release archive with its checksum.

Documentation checks cover model/field presence, navigation and links, frozen versions and public content. The release workflow also runs the existing runtime, restart and packaging checks before publishing artifacts. Reference coverage checks establish structural presence; descriptions and defaults still require source review.

See the release comparison.

docs.title: Recorded fixture measurements
docs.text: The September 30 platform run used one Kind host, two allowed drivers, one request slot per driver and 0–2 one-core executors per driver. Both roles used 512m heap plus 384m overhead. Executor idle/cache/shuffle timeouts were 5s/8s/8s; driver idle was 120s.

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text:
Observation Recorded value Durable acceptance, seven submissions 2.96–4.99 ms Four load-job queue waits 7.44s, 7.47s, 37.84s, 38.04s Peak drivers / executors / simultaneous requests 2 / 4 / 2 Retained request RDDs after completion 0 Additional wait for executor retirement after the UI/cache check 4.24s Additional wait for idle driver retirement after later checks 107.44s

Polling began after other checks, so these retirement observations are not exact time from the final Spark task. They are fixture measurements, not capacity or latency promises.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
PostgreSQL/S3 restarts, API replica replacement and complete driver shutdown preserved local/S3 result access. Signed-token tests checked cryptographic identity rules separately. The fixture did not certify production IAM, multi-node storage failure or load at result-size/part-count ceilings.

Executable groups include e2e.py, platform-results-e2e.py, platform-fault-e2e.py, platform-load-e2e.py, platform-final-smoke.py, pod-template-e2e.py and test-helm.py. See validation scope and acceptance coverage.

Generated request IDs, image digests and raw run logs stay outside Git. CI can retain them as run artifacts when needed.
